Only one of the five comments points at a real bug: #3, which is a privilege escalation. The other four are cosmetic nits in the new test file. I wrote the verdicts to `verdicts.json` and made no code changes.

| # | Issue | Category | Verdict | Actionable |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Typo "initializaed" | NITPICK | VALID | OPTIONAL |
| 1 | Line with only whitespace | NITPICK | VALID | OPTIONAL |
| 2 | Copyright year 2024 vs 2025 | CONVENTION | STYLE_PREFERENCE | OPTIONAL |
| 3 | `canManage()` also accepts the VIEW permission | SECURITY / CORRECTNESS | VALID | **YES** |
| 4 | Double semicolon | NITPICK | VALID | OPTIONAL |

**#3 (the one that matters):**
- **The bug:** at `GroupPermissionsV2.java:70`, `canManage()` calls `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`. `hasPermission` (lines 151–160) returns true if *any* of the listed permissions is granted.
- **Who it affects:** an admin given only the view permission on all groups passes `canManage()`.
- **What they can do:** `GroupsResource.java:181` (`addTopLevelGroup`) relies on `requireManage()`, so that admin can create top-level groups.
- **It's inconsistent with the rest of the code:** the single-group check `canManage(GroupModel)` at line 79 accepts only MANAGE. The old V1 version (`GroupPermissions.java:274`) also allowed only admins with the manage-users role.
- **Fix:** check only MANAGE on line 70.

**The other four:**
- **#0, #1, #4** are all real but harmless. They are in `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java`: the typo at line 70, the whitespace-only line at 300, and the `;;` at line 68.
- **#2:** the test files in the same package use both 2024 and 2025, so there's no convention for the header year to break.
